failure_summary: The assembled L7 guardrail contradicts itself — it orders 'Explain the blunder through the opening — book line, centrality, parity' and lists 'central' as approved vocabulary, then forbids saying either column is 'more central' (openingContext.defense.centralityGrounded=false) — and all 5 runs took the invitation, resting the explanation on a board-false central-grip claim (visualize_board on 33333111155: col2 and col6 are symmetric about the centre and the MOST central legal column, col4, scores -2, worse than col6's -1), leaving A7 with only an outcome restatement ('they finish the practical race faster').
notes: Sub-sampling per rubric: A3/A4/G2/G4/G5 graded on runs 0-1 only, null (not scored) on runs 2-4; A5/A7 graded on all 5. | A1/A2/A6 and G7a/G7b_offered copied verbatim from *_mechanical.json (all pass, all 5 runs); annotationRepairs empty in all 5. | A4 fail runs 0-1: 'the toughest central setup' (run 0) / 'this was an opening choice about centrality' + 'keep the central-column shape' (run 1) assert a centrality edge for column 6 over column 2 that the board refutes (equidistant from centre; scr row gives c4=-2 vs c6=-1) and that the vector explicitly withholds (centralityGrounded=false). Same wording recurs in runs 2-4 ('give up that central structure', 'that central grip', 'steadier central grip') but A4 was not scored there. | G2(a) fail runs 0-1: the guardrail clause 'do not say one column is more central ... unless this vector gives you that comparison' is breached verbatim. | A5a fail run 0 only: prose writes raw cell notation 'the key square c5r4' and 'on c7r3' — the render's own rule is 'Never write a raw square' (known OI-194). A5b (player 2 + opening) PASSES on all 5: every run frames column 6 as the most stubborn defense keeping the practical swindle alive, none says the player is lost. | A7 fail 5/5, subtests A7a+A7d: once the false centrality idea is set aside, the operative reason in every run is an outcome/race restatement ('so they finish the practical race faster' r0, 'reach the late square ... faster' r1, 'let their forced line arrive sooner' r2, 'comes into play first' r3, 'let the position resolve faster for your opponent' r4), with the deep squares tagged but never explained. The real cause WAS in the prompt and unused by all 5 — replyHistogram afterBest=1 vs afterPlayed=7, surfaced as 'one slip by your opponent (watch columns 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7) could let you climb back in' — but it is not in the required set, so this is render_bug per the A7 triage rule, not a model failure. A7b passes (every specific-sounding referent is inside an emitted zone); A7c N/A (no fork; no *-fork-pivot alias offered). | G4/G5 pass runs 0-1: the two named resources are board-true on the engine's own lines — projectedDeep (lostResource.finalMovestring) has Y at c3r4,c4r4,c6r4 with c5r4 completing your row-4 four, projectedDeepOpp (render_decision.finalMovestring 333331111551530000001244442222244565566) has O at c4r3,c5r3,c6r3 with c7r3 completing; all three rendered tactic entries (immediate c5r5 opp, major c5r6 you, immediate c7r4 you) check out on their stated boards. No alternate PV was used. | G7 fail run 4 only: [zone:future:windows:c3r4,c4r4,c5r4,c6r4] (role: YOUR line, truthBoard projectedDeep) is bound to 'their later key square and four-in-a-row line', giving the line the wrong owner — a semantically wrong phrase for the handle's role. Run 3 has a milder version of the same ownership blur and is passed. | Required-set omission recorded, NOT charged: runs 1, 3 and 4 never emit the required [zone:future:c5r4] (you-key-square). The harness calls the model once; production retries on a missing required handle, so this is an eval artifact of OI-183, not evidence that enforcement is absent. | Production-fidelity caveat: model is gpt-5.4-mini, the model production ships, so any prompt_confusion reading here cannot be separated from model capability — the decisive attribution chosen (the self-contradicting centrality guardrail) is model-independent.
